channel.title: Loose Ends blog
channel.description: Notes from Loose Ends on AI assistants, connections, automation and visibility in search and AI answers.

item.title: What Is MCP? Model Context Protocol in Plain Language
item.description: MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is an open standard that lets AI assistants reach a firm's tools and data. How a connector works, and what to connect first.

item.title: Claude Setup for Teams: Working From the Firm's Own Data
item.description: Setting up Claude for a team means a shared workspace, projects that hold the firm's context, connections to its tools, reusable instructions and training.

item.title: AI Assistant Adoption Gap: Why Teams Use So Little of It
item.description: Most teams use a fraction of their AI assistant because of the blank page, no access to the firm's data, no shared instructions and no owner. Each has a fix.

item.title: Connect Claude to a Recruiting Database Such as Loxo
item.description: Connecting Claude to a recruiting database such as Loxo lets a search firm's team question its own candidate data in plain language, with access controlled.

item.title: Custom API Integration When No Connector Exists
item.description: When a tool has no ready connector, a custom integration can be built against its API. What that involves, the risks, the upkeep, and who owns the result.

item.title: Automate enquiry follow-up so no quote goes quiet
item.description: Enquiry follow-up can be automated. A system reads the inbox, quotes and invoices, finds what went quiet and drafts replies a person approves before sending.

item.title: Automate invoice reminders with a person approving each one
item.description: Invoice reminders can run on a schedule. The system checks the accounting tool, drafts a reminder for each stage, and a person approves it before it goes out.

item.title: Booking confirmation and reminder automation, explained
item.description: Booking confirmations, reminders and rescheduling can run by themselves once bookings live in one place instead of in direct messages. Here's how it works.

item.title: Human-in-the-loop automation: approve before it sends
item.description: Human-in-the-loop automation means the system drafts and a person approves before anything reaches a client. Where approval sits, and what never to automate.

item.title: Automate weekly reporting: figures ready before anyone asks
item.description: Weekly reporting can be automated by pulling figures from existing tools into one dashboard and sending the team a short summary in Slack or email each week.

item.title: AI Candidate Screening With Reasoning Behind Every Score
item.description: AI candidate screening works when every score shows its reasoning and the source text from the résumé, so the recruiter can check it and make the decision.

item.title: Sync Job Listings From an ATS to the Firm's Website
item.description: Open roles can be entered once in the firm's recruiting system and appear on its website automatically, with no retyping. CVs can be reformatted in one step.

item.title: Interview Notes to Client Report, Every Rating Sourced
item.description: Raw interview notes can become a finished client report in the firm's format, with every rating pointing to its source and gaps flagged, never filled in.

item.title: Shopify Etsy Inventory Sync Without Selling Twice
item.description: Shopify and Etsy inventory stays in sync when stock lives in one place and every sale updates it, so an item is never sold twice and nothing is retyped.

item.title: Booking App Instead of Instagram Messages: Why Switch
item.description: A business that takes bookings through Instagram or WhatsApp messages should move them to one booking screen showing schedule, places, payment and language.

item.title: Generative engine optimization (GEO): how firms get cited
item.description: GEO makes a firm easy for ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google's AI answers to find and quote, using answer-first pages, consistent facts and open crawling.

item.title: Structured data and llms.txt: what each one does
item.description: Structured data tells search engines and assistants what a page is about; llms.txt gives them a plain-text summary. Neither guarantees ranking or citation.

item.title: Content system: one idea into an article and a week of posts
item.description: A content system turns one idea into a researched article and a week of posts for Substack, LinkedIn and Instagram, every figure checked against a source.

item.title: AI assistant for journalists: an editorial week around video
item.description: An AI assistant for journalists can take on the repeated preparation around video, from research notes to captions, while editorial judgement stays human.

item.title: Brand identity for a guesthouse, drawn from the building
item.description: A guesthouse brand identity drawn from the building's tiles, doors and objects, carried through a bilingual website and the printed pieces guests hold.

item.title: Connect Slack to Claude: approvals, alerts and answers
item.description: Connecting Slack to Claude puts approvals, alerts and questions where the team already talks, with each person seeing only what their own access allows.

item.title: Client onboarding automation without the paperwork chase
item.description: Client onboarding automation collects forms, documents and signatures, files them, drafts reminders for what's missing and tells the team when it's all in.

item.title: Meeting notes to CRM actions: summaries, decisions, owners
item.description: Meeting notes to CRM actions: each call is summarized, decisions and next steps go into the CRM, owners get reminded, and people keep the decisions.

item.title: AI document filing automation: read, named and filed
item.description: AI document filing reads email attachments and uploads, names each file by the firm's rules and files it in the right folder or record, with an audit trail.

item.title: Substack newsletter automation: a draft that writes itself
item.description: Substack newsletter automation gathers the week's articles and updates into a draft in the firm's voice, ready for a person to review and send.

item.title: AI automation cost: what a firm pays and what drives it
item.description: AI automation at Loose Ends starts from $3,000 at a fixed price agreed in writing. Scope, tools, approval steps, data quality and upkeep set the final figure.

item.title: Systems audit before automation: why it comes first
item.description: A systems audit finds where a firm's week goes and ranks fixes by what they return, before any build. At Loose Ends it costs $1,500, credited to the build.

item.title: Claude vs ChatGPT for business teams: how to choose
item.description: Claude or ChatGPT for a team? Both can do the work. What decides the result is the link to the firm's data, shared instructions, permissions and training.

item.title: Website that books clients: turning visitors into bookings
item.description: A website that books clients answers questions plainly, offers a booking path tied to the calendar and inbox, follows up, and is found in search and AI.

item.title: AI for recruiting firms: using it responsibly in a search
item.description: AI helps a recruiting firm with sourcing notes, CV formatting, assessment with reasoning, outreach drafts and client reports, while the recruiter decides.

item.title: Claude Skills for Business: What They Are and How to Use Them
item.description: A Claude skill is a packaged set of instructions Claude loads when a task needs it, so a weekly report or proposal runs the same way for anyone on the team.
